title: UPDATED: Jail cell death leads to guilty plea
article: Orangeville Sgt. Chris Dryden has pleaded guilty to two counts of discreditable conduct in relation to the jail cell death of Adam Sprague.
Dryden entered the plea during a Police Service Act (PSA) hearing held Monday (June 11).

"He didn't ask for details of the arrest of Adam Sprague, which would have shown that the arrest was unlawful," prosecutor Ian Johnstone said, while explaining the charges. "The second discreditable conduct, he failed to check on the well-being of prisoners while they were in the cell area."

The sergeant originally faced five PSA charges - three of discreditable conduct and two for insubordination - following an investigation by the Hamilton Police Service. The other three charges Dryden faced have been withdrawn.
Sprague, 25, died of a drug overdose while in a holding cell at the C Line police station early in the morning of Nov. 11, 2010.

Orangeville Police Service Chief Joe Tomei ordered the parallel investigation in April 2011, after the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) announced no criminal charges would be laid in relation to Sprague's death.
The SIU did criticize Dryden for not physically checking on Sprague throughout the night.
The department, Tomei, Dryden, Sgt. Lindsay White, Const. Jon Kennedy, Const. Jason Moore and two unnamed police civilians face a more than $1.5 million lawsuit filed by Sprague's family.
Kennedy pleaded guilty earlier this year to discreditable conduct during a PSA hearing regarding Sprague's arrest and was ordered to serve 24 hours of unpaid duty.
Dryden's tribunal will reconvene on July 6 for sentencing.
